title: The First Modern Olympic Games
passages: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in the spring of 1896. They were the dream of Pierre de Coubertin, a French ARISTOCRAT who loved sport and believed it could bring young people from many countries together. Coubertin wanted to REVIVE the famous games of ancient Greece, which had ended more than 1,500 years earlier. In 1894 he gathered supporters at a meeting in Paris, and together they formed the International Olympic Committee. Greece was chosen as the first host, a fitting choice for the land where the Olympic story had begun nearly 3,000 years ago.

The Games ran from April 6 to April 15, 1896. About 241 athletes from 14 nations took part, all of them men, competing in 43 events such as running, swimming, wrestling and cycling. Many events took place in the PANATHENAIC Stadium, an ancient arena rebuilt in gleaming white marble. On the first day, an American named James Connolly won the triple jump and became the first modern Olympic champion. The proudest moment for Greece came in the MARATHON, when a local water carrier named Spyridon Louis crossed the finish line first. Tens of thousands of fans cheered as winners received a silver medal and an olive branch.
